questions.question: Give the formula of chlorophyll and explain the role of magnesium in plants. What happens if there is a deficiency of magnesium in the soil?
questions.solution:
**Formula.** Chlorophyll has the molecular formula $C_{55}H_{72}MgN_4O_5$; chlorophyll a is $C_{55}H_{72}MgN_4O_5$ and chlorophyll b is $C_{55}H_{70}MgN_4O_6$.

**Structure and the role of Mg.** The chlorophyll molecule consists of a porphyrin ring containing four nitrogen atoms. At the centre of this ring sits a single $Mg^{2+}$ ion, which is held by coordinate bonds to the four pyrrole nitrogens of the ring. This $Mg^{2+}$ ion is essential for the chlorophyll molecule to absorb light, and through it chlorophyll carries out **photosynthesis**, converting solar energy into chemical energy in the synthesis of carbohydrates.

**Deficiency.** Magnesium is a **mobile** nutrient. When it is deficient in the soil, it is withdrawn from the older leaves and translocated to the young growing leaves. Consequently the older leaves lose their green colour and become pale yellow — this yellowing is called **chlorosis** — and the plant's growth and photosynthetic output fall, ultimately causing **stunted growth** and early leaf fall. Adding magnesium sulphate or dolomite to the soil restores the green colour.
questions.knowledgeNote: Chlorophyll C₅₅H₇₂MgN₄O₅ has a central Mg²⁺ ion; its deficiency causes chlorosis of the older leaves.
